checker.tool: Codex desktop exec_command/apply_patch with frozen rustuml and diff_one binaries

java_locations.finding: Quark qualified names are canonical quark codes joined through the owning parent with Plasma's separator.
UGroup.put applies fix(), replacing every character matched by [^-\w ] with a dot before SVG metadata serialization.

Container declarations ending in '{' accept broader code forms than CommandCreateElementFull: quoted display-first CODE1 is ([^#%s{}]+), bare CODE9 is ([^#%s{}%g]*). Hyphen and slash are valid canonical codes for deployment containers.
Named notes use diagram.quarkInContext(false, cleanId(idShort)); when declared inside a group their SVG data-qualified-name inherits the owning quark.
Link metadata uses endpoint entity names and UIDs, so endpoint identity must survive parser alias handling.

rust_locations.finding: RE_NODE_BARE and RE_NODE_QUOTED are not end-anchored and use narrower id grammars than CommandPackageWithUSymbol. They can partially consume valid Java container codes.

Quoted deployment declarations take caps[3] as the canonical id when present. For `as tenant-a`, caps[3] becomes `tenant` because the regex stops before the hyphen and the trailing text is not rejected.
The shared UGroup projection itself matches the cited Java fix rule for ASCII word, space, and hyphen. The rejection is not due to this projection helper.
Deployment qnames are built from parsed node IDs and parent ownership, so any parser-side canonical-code truncation propagates into cluster, leaf, note, and link metadata.

inputs.finding: Java accepts `cloud zone/prod {` as a deployment container and projects the slash to `zone.prod`. Rust renders the same valid source as an empty STATE diagram, so the claimed deployment SVG qname mechanism is not robust across Java's container identity grammar.

reason: The implementation projects parsed IDs correctly only after the parser has captured the right canonical quark code. Java-valid deployment container codes containing hyphen or slash are accepted by CommandPackageWithUSymbol but are truncated or missed by Rust's deployment declaration grammar. The resulting owner identity mismatch propagates into cluster, leaf, named-note, and link metadata. Both failing inputs are preserved with Java SVGs and Rust/diff evidence.
